Have you ever zoned out on a Zoom call, then realised you’ve missed the last two minutes? I’ve been trying Wispr Flow’s Notetaker, which records and transcribes meetings in real time. You can ask it what you missed, search previous meetings for specific decisions, and use the transcripts with tools like ChatGPT and Claude to draft follow-up emails or messages. Very useful if, like me, you spend a lot of time in meetings, and even more time trying to remember what actually happened in them.  It’s currently available on Mac and Windows, and the Notetaker is free to use. Copy the link for one month of Wispr Flow Pro for free: https://ref.wisprflow.ai/ali_tiktok_notetaker

If you're struggling to figure out what to do with your life, try the Odyssey Plan. It's an exercise that Stanford Business School uses to help people figure out their path. You ask yourself three questions: 1️⃣ Your current path: If you continued down your current path, what would your life look like 5 years from now? 2️⃣ Your alternative path: If you had to take a completely different path, what would your life look like 5 years from now? 3️⃣ Your radical path: If you took a completely different path but didn't care what anyone thought and weren't worried about money, what would your life look like? I don't lift to be smaller. I lift because the woman I'll be at 80 is depending on the choices I make at 58, and I'd like to hand her a body that can still get up off the floor, carry her own groceries, and board a plane without someone holding her elbow. Here's what changes in midlife: as estrogen falls through the menopause transition, women lose muscle and bone faster, insulin resistance climbs, and visceral fat starts to accumulate. Resistance training is one of the few interventions that pushes back on all four at once (and no, it won't make you bulky; it makes you harder to break). You don't need a perfect program. The menopause guideline most OB-GYNs have practiced under was written in 2014, before the newest nonhormonal drugs existed and before the FDA changed the hormone therapy label. On October 15, ACOG replaced it: Clinical Practice Guideline No. 13, published in Obstetrics & Gynecology (2026), covering hot flushes, sleep, and mood. Hormone therapy is strongly recommended for hot flushes and the sleep disruption they cause, started before 60 or within 10 years of menopause; continuing past 60 may be necessary if symptoms persist.
